newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico debt issues draw yield-hungry mark buyers.
newsitem.headline: Mexico debt issues draw yield-hungry mark buyers.

text.p: Mexican debt issuers, along with other emerging borrowers, are finding a ready market in yield-hungry investors in German marks, bond analysts said.
The latest example is the Mexican government, which on Monday added 500 million marks to its issue due September 2004, increasing the size of the deal to 1.5 billion marks.

"What happened is that the placement made in August was over-subscribed, so the Mexican government decided to take advantage of this to increase the placement," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's chief economist in Mexico, Oscar Vera.
"It is not only the German market. All the global placements that have been made, in Japan as well, have shown an excess of demand. They have been well received," Vera said.
With low yields in their home countries, many private overseas investors are looking to emerging markets such as Mexico for higher returns, analysts said.

"You have got Deutsche mark investors stretching for yield, so it is smart for the Mexican government to tap that low-yielding market," said Gary Evans, senior fixed income strategist with Lehman Brothers.
"The Japanese and the Germans have historically low interest rates, and those low rates are now pushing investors down the credit spectrum and into emerging markets," he added.
Merrill Lynch noted in a recent report that the U.S. dollar made up 82 percent of emerging market debut issuances in 1994 before dropping to 49 percent in 1995.
Meanwhile, mark issues went from five percent in 1994 to 17 percent in 1995 and continued to rise in the first few months of 1996. Yen issues also rose.
Among Mexican borrowers, mark issues have been popular.
In August, 1995, development bank Nacional Financiera placed a 250 million three-year mark issue.
Last November, the Mexican federal government placed a five-year 1.0 billion mark issue at 407 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
In January, it followed with a seven-year mark issue worth about 1.5 billion marks at 491 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
During the second quarter, development bank Bancomext placed a three-year issue worth $203.8 million at Libor plus 325 basis points.
